craft_evidence.owned: yes (brand statement + own film): ready-to-wear made in its own Northampton workshop, filmed with named artisans (Lopez: Behind the Craft); Hermès-owned since 1976; press (Modaes, 5 Jun 2026) reports a new Northampton plant by 2029; no street address or filing read
craft_evidence.makers: self only: PDPs and our-story say made in its Northampton workshop; trainers stated Made in Italy with no maker named (Court)
craft_evidence.mills: no: leathers named by house type (Oxford calf, Museum calf, Gentle Calf, Bristle Hide, Dew Hide); no tannery named; sole guide says vegetable-tanned full grain leather, tannery unnamed
craft_evidence.madein: 6 of 6 sampled PDPs state country (Lopez 75, Bill, Tyne II, Foil, Sommet: Made in England; Court trainer: Made in Italy); Foundry II PDP did not render
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: founder walked from Cornwall to London 1851; bootmaker to the Prince of Wales 1863; first bespoke boutique Regent Street 1866; Paris 1899; Hermès 1976; ready-to-wear 1982
craft_evidence.process: yes: 190-step process over several weeks in Northampton; Goodyear welt, Blake, Norwegian construction named per PDP; sole guide documents closed-channel lock stitching and vegetable-tanned soles; workshop film follows each step of the Lopez
craft_evidence.reasoning: John Lobb states its ready-to-wear is made in its own Northampton workshop in a 190-step process, documents construction per PDP and shows the workshop and named artisans in its own film; heritage is dated and placed (1866 London, 1899 Paris). Held at 4 not 5: trainers are Made in Italy with no maker named, no tannery is named, and the owned workshop rests on brand statements and press rather than a filing read; a 5 is defensible if the trainers do not weigh.
